one_line: A Chandela royal lady and her samanta allies shaping land, temples and trade in 11th-century Jejakabhukti.

appearance.age_look: late 20s, medium height, poised but sturdy build suggesting travel and administrative work rather than battlefield combat
appearance.face: oval face with soft but defined jaw, medium-brown north Indian complexion, large sharp anime eyes with slightly arched brows, a small straight nose, and a calm yet analytical default expression as if weighing documents and people at once
appearance.hair: long black hair oiled and gathered into a single thick braid falling down her back, center-parted at the front with a smooth hairline; braid wrapped at the end with a narrow gold band; she wears a simple narrow gold circlet across the forehead (no high crown), and small round gold earrings
appearance.costume: era-accurate 10th–11th century central Indian royal woman’s dress: a deep-maroon ankle‑length wrapped lower garment (like a tightly draped antariya) with a subtle thin gold border, pleats falling slightly to her left; a fitted half‑sleeve blouse in muted leaf‑green cotton under a rich saffron‑gold fine cotton or light silk upper cloth (uttariya) diagonally draped from left shoulder across the torso and around the waist, covering chest and midriff completely; a narrow maroon and gold waistband cord with a small central gold clasp, a few thin gold bangles on each wrist, a simple short gold necklace close to the neck, and plain leather sandals suited for palace courtyards and temple visits; fabrics look hand‑woven with very subtle stripe or check textures but no heavy ornamentation, emphasizing practical dignity over ostentatious luxury
appearance.signature: a rolled copper-plate grant tied with a narrow cord and a small circular seal, carried in her left hand or tucked at her waist, sometimes being unrolled while she gestures with her right hand toward an imagined landscape of fields, temples and trade routes

ref_desc: Satyabhama is a late‑20s Chandela noblewoman with an oval medium‑brown face, large sharp eyes, long black braided hair with a simple gold circlet, wearing a deep‑maroon wrapped skirt, leaf‑green blouse, saffron‑gold draped shawl, modest gold jewellery, and holding a rolled copper‑plate grant sealed with a small circular seal.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Satyabhama, a late-20s Chandela-era noblewoman from 10th–11th century central India, shown front, three-quarter, and back: she has an oval medium-brown face, large sharp eyes with thoughtful brows, and long black hair neatly center-parted and gathered into a single thick braid down her back, the braid tip bound with a narrow gold band; a simple narrow gold circlet rests across her forehead and she wears small round gold earrings, a short plain gold necklace, a few thin gold bangles, and no heavy crown. Her clothing is fully modest and historically grounded: an ankle-length deep-maroon wrapped lower garment with a thin gold border and soft pleats to the left; a fitted half-sleeve blouse in muted leaf-green cotton; and a saffron-gold fine cotton or light silk upper cloth draped from her left shoulder across her torso and around her waist, covering chest and midriff completely, with the end hanging gracefully but practically. A slim maroon and gold cord belt with a small central gold clasp encircles her waist, and she wears simple brown leather sandals. Her signature prop is a rolled copper-plate grant tied with a cord and a small circular seal, sometimes held in her left hand, sometimes tucked at her waist, while her right hand gestures as if explaining land, temples and trade routes; emphasize the deep maroon, saffron-gold, leaf green, warm brown and dull gold palette, and keep her posture dignified, calm and authoritative rather than martial.
